You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 580e4273d7a883ececfefa692c1f96bdbacb99b5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Cong Wang <xiyou.wangcong@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2020 12:13:34 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] net_sched: check error pointer in tcf_dump_walker()

Although we take RTNL on dump path, it is possible to
skip RTNL on insertion path. So the following race condition
is possible:

rtnl_lock()		// no rtnl lock
			mutex_lock(&idrinfo->lock);
			// insert ERR_PTR(-EBUSY)
			mutex_unlock(&idrinfo->lock);
tc_dump_action()
rtnl_unlock()

So we have to skip those temporary -EBUSY entries on dump path
too.

Reported-and-tested-by: syzbot+b47bc4f247856fb4d9e1@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Fixes: 0fedc63fadf0 ("net_sched: commit action insertions together")
Cc: Vlad Buslov <vladbu@mellanox.com>
Cc: Jamal Hadi Salim <jhs@mojatatu.com>
Cc: Jiri Pirko <jiri@resnulli.us>
Signed-off-by: Cong Wang <xiyou.wangcong@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/sched/act_api.c b/net/sched/act_api.c
index 5612b336e18e..798430e1a79f 100644
--- a/net/sched/act_api.c
+++ b/net/sched/act_api.c
@@ -235,6 +235,8 @@ static int tcf_dump_walker(struct tcf_idrinfo *idrinfo, struct sk_buff *skb,
 		index++;
 		if (index < s_i)
 			continue;
+		if (IS_ERR(p))
+			continue;
 
 		if (jiffy_since &&
 		    time_after(jiffy_since,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/sched/act_api.c`**
   - A check for error pointers was added in the `tcf_dump_walker` function. Specifically, the following lines were introduced:
     ```c
     if (IS_ERR(p))
         continue;
     ```
   - This modification ensures that if the pointer `p` is an error pointer (i.e., it contains an error code), the function will skip processing that entry.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `net/sched/act_api.c` addresses a race condition that can occur when the insertion path does not hold the RTNL lock, allowing for the insertion of an error pointer (`ERR_PTR(-EBUSY)`). By adding the check for error pointers in the dump path, the patch prevents the function from processing these temporary error entries, thereby ensuring the integrity of the dump operation and avoiding potential issues that could arise from handling invalid data. This change is a direct response to the reported bug and is aimed at improving the robustness of the network scheduling code.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
// insert ERR_PTR(-EBUSY)
```
```c
if (index < s_i)
```
```c
// no rtnl lock
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the RTNL lock is not held during the insertion path, allowing an error pointer (`ERR_PTR(-EBUSY)`) to be inserted into the data structure. When the dump path is executed, it may encounter this error pointer without any checks, leading to incorrect processing or crashes.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (IS_ERR(p))
```
```c
continue;
```
Reason:
The fix introduces a check for error pointers in the dump function. By adding `if (IS_ERR(p)) continue;`, the code ensures that any invalid entries (like `ERR_PTR(-EBUSY)`) are skipped during the dump process, preventing incorrect processing and potential crashes.
